findings.claim: Contractless string-key mode generates a formatter that deserializes into a type from a referenced assembly. In the generated code path, members are created with IsWritable/IsReadable hard-coded true and nestedFormatterRequired false. Nothing in this change applies MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData handling to the surrogate or contractless path, and the changed templates do not alter this. This is consistent with existing generator behavior, so the main risk is that members with types lacking formatters are not flagged (reportDiagnostic is null in the generation pass). Unsupported member types can fall through to runtime resolver lookups instead of being rejected at compile time.

receipt_plan.detail: Read CreateMember: IsWritable/IsReadable are hard-coded true and CustomFormatter is null. Confirm that the generated code uses options.Resolver.GetFormatterWithVerify, which honors MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and the depth limit via options.Security.DepthStep. No change in this diff disables those protections, so this is an unverified hunch.
